findings.paper_title: Commercial Commissioning and Procurement Strategy - Appendix
findings.headline: Council has implemented enhanced procurement controls including a £500,000 Procurement Gateway, supplier financial risk checks, and a new contract management system.
findings.detail: The council has strengthened its control environment through several initiatives: a new corporate contract management system, supplier financial risk assessments introduced for medium and high-value contracts, a £500,000 Procurement Gateway to screen procurements, publication of a bi-annual procurement pipeline, and mandatory training on the Procurement Act 2023. These process improvements support the council's ability to identify and manage commercial risks earlier and more consistently.
findings.matters: Enhanced procurement controls and supplier financial checks reduce the risk of service disruption or financial loss from supplier failure or poor contract performance; they are indicators of operational risk management maturity.
findings.figures: £500,000 Procurement Gateway threshold
findings.quote: Processes have been strengthened through supplier financial checks, a £500,000 Procurement Gateway, and publication of a biannual procurement pipeline.

findings.paper_title: Commercial Commissioning and Procurement Strategy - Appendix
findings.headline: Internal and External Audit opinions on procurement compliance and governance have improved and are now stable.
findings.detail: The council reports that performance improvements are reflected in stable and improved Internal Audit opinions on procurement compliance and governance, and an improved External Audit opinion. These improvements follow establishment of the Commissioning and Commercial Board, development of new processes, and training on procurement compliance and risk management.
findings.matters: Audit opinions on financial controls and procurement governance are a leading indicator of control environment quality; improved audit opinions reduce the risk of financial surprise, service disruption or compliance failure.
findings.figures: None; audit opinions are qualitative assessments
findings.quote: Improved performance is reflected in stable and improved Internal Audit opinions of procurement compliance and governance as well as an improved External Audit opinion.

findings.paper_title: Commercial Commissioning and Procurement Strategy - Appendix
findings.headline: Strategy is explicitly short-term in scope due to expected Local Government Reorganisation in the medium term, with LGR becoming an increasing focus during the strategy period.
findings.detail: The council's strategy is focused on the short term because of the expectation of local government reorganisation in the medium term. The council states that LGR will become an increasingly prominent focus during the life of this strategy, and that commercial priorities must support a smooth transition to new arrangements. This creates a period of organisational uncertainty that could impact service continuity and financial performance.
findings.matters: Local Government Reorganisation is a material structural change that creates uncertainty in service delivery, contract continuity, and management focus; councils transitioning through LGR face elevated operational risk during the change period.
findings.figures: None; LGR timing is not quantified
findings.quote: The Strategy is focused on the short term due to the expectation of local government re-organisation in the medium term. However, its priorities and focus will support a commercial focused transition to those new arrangements and LGR will become an increasing focus during the life of this strategy.

findings.paper_title: Commercial Commissioning and Procurement Strategy - Appendix
findings.headline: Council strategy explicitly targets increased commercial income and trading returns to reduce the level of financial savings required to balance the budget.
findings.detail: The council states it is seeking to increase income streams from commercial investments, fees, charges and traded services to reduce the level of financial savings needed. The council's balanced budget is dependent on this income. The strategy includes objectives to maximize returns from existing property, land and traded services as a means of addressing the funding gap, making commercial revenue success a material factor in budget stability.
findings.matters: A council that depends on commercial revenues for budget balance has greater sensitivity to commercial activity success or failure; the council is explicitly budgeting some of its gap closure to commercial returns rather than to external funding or reserves.
findings.figures: £600m to £800m annual spend with third parties; £1.3b gross annual budget
findings.quote: We will be seeking to increase income streams into the Council to reduce the level of financial savings it will need to make, which will in turn help the Council invest in priority services.

findings.paper_title: Commercial Commissioning and Procurement Strategy - Appendix
findings.headline: Targeted reviews of high-overspend areas have identified £8.4m in savings, with £1.5m delivered to date; case studies show an additional £5.236m identified through specific service reviews.
findings.detail: The council has conducted focused reviews of high-overspend areas that identified £8.4m in total savings, of which £1.5m has been delivered to date. Three case studies illustrate further identified savings: Out of School Tuition (£2.076m annual savings/cost avoidance potential), Enhanced Personal Transport Budget (£2.64m annual savings potential), and Older People Block Beds (£520,635 financial recovery). This demonstrates active management of financial pressures through detailed procurement and commissioning analysis.
findings.matters: Tangible delivery of identified savings demonstrates active financial management and budget discipline; the proportion delivered and additional opportunities identified are indicators of whether the council is managing toward or away from its funding gap.
findings.figures: £8.4m identified; £1.5m delivered to date; £2.076m Out of School Tuition; £2.64m Personal Transport Budget; £520,635 Older People Block Beds
findings.quote: Targeted reviews of high-overspend areas have identified £8.4m in savings, with £1.5m delivered to date.

findings.paper_title: Commercial Commissioning and Procurement Strategy - Appendix
findings.headline: The Council faces a growing funding gap with £57m of pressure funding applied to the 2026/27 budget; Fair Funding Allocation is the seventh lowest among shire authorities at £275 per resident.
findings.detail: Cambridgeshire reports it continues to face financial pressures, with Fair Funding Allocation remaining low even among shire authorities. The council applied £57m of pressure funding to the 2026/27 budget to address inflation and demand pressures. The council's Medium Term Financial Plan highlights a growing funding gap that this strategy is intended to help close.
findings.matters: A council with a structural funding gap that requires savings or relies on non-core revenues for budget balance is a material credit consideration for lenders; the direction and magnitude of the gap signals financial sustainability risks.
findings.figures: £57m pressure funding for 2026/27; £275 per resident fair funding allocation; seventh lowest among shire authorities
findings.quote: The Council continues to face financial pressures. Cambridgeshire's Fair Funding Allocation remains low even among shire authorities, being the seventh lowest at £275 per resident. In addition, we are facing both inflation and demand pressures on the budget, overall £57m of pressure funding was applied to the 2026/27 budget.

findings.headline: Council cites financial and structural position changes as rationale for strategy revision; specifics not disclosed
findings.detail: The strategy update was prompted by "changes in the structural and financial position of the Council" alongside Procurement Act 2023 implementation, but the paper does not specify what these changes were, their direction, or scale. The resulting strategy emphasizes commercial focus, cost avoidance, and savings to support financial stability.
findings.matters: Council financial position changes can signal emerging pressures; the strategy revision indicates something material has shifted, prompting management response, though details must be sought elsewhere
findings.quote: changes in the structural and financial position of the Council mean that it is timely to update and revise the strategy

findings.headline: Council identifies Local Government Reorganisation as potential outcome requiring strategic preparation
findings.detail: The revised commercial strategy explicitly lists, if required, preparation for LGR as an outcome alongside improved commercial practice and cost avoidance. The council notes that despite ongoing LGR reviews, these do not currently impact the strategy's focus, indicating the council is positioning itself for a potential restructuring while continuing with current initiatives.
findings.matters: LGR fundamentally changes council governance and financial structure; lenders and peer councils monitor which councils are explicitly preparing for possible structural reorganisation
findings.quote: This focus will in turn drive savings, improved practice and, if required, preparation for LGR.

findings.headline: Commercial property investment income returned 5.3% against a 6% target in Q1 2026/27.
findings.detail: This represents an improvement from 4% in the prior quarter, with commercial properties remaining highly occupied and rents rising. The council has acknowledged that achieving the 6% target is unlikely without a radical review of the commercial estate, citing global geopolitical events as a constraint. Officers are pursuing specific remedial actions including assessing This Land's business plan, completing outstanding rent reviews, and conducting a full estate review to be presented in October.
findings.matters: A lender needs to assess the sustainability of commercial property income as a revenue stream and understand any structural constraints on its performance, particularly given the council's significant prior investment in this area.
findings.quote: Performance for quarter 1 was 5.3% against a target of 6%. Global geopolitical events mean it is unlikely the Council will be able to achieve a pathway to achieving 6% going forward without a radical review of the estate.

findings.headline: POhWER out-of-county advocacy services (£60,000) delivered via non-compliant spot purchasing for Mental Capacity Act duties; contract variation planned for February 2027
findings.detail: The council's POhWER contract covers in-county advocacy only, but out-of-county services are required to meet statutory Deprivation of Liberty Safeguards responsibilities. These have been commissioned via spot purchasing, triggering a breach report. A contract variation is being developed to formally incorporate out-of-county services from February 2027.
findings.matters: Illustrates a council managing a gap between contracted scope and statutory duty delivery while moving toward compliant procurement; shows how operational pressures intersect with compliance requirements.
findings.figures: £60,000 (POhWER breach); February 2027 implementation date
findings.quote: The existing contract with POhWER covers in-county advocacy only, so, in order to maintain delivery of our statutory duties under the Mental Capacity Act 2005 and Deprivation of Liberty Safeguards (DoLS) responsibilities, out-of-county services have continued to be commissioned via spot purchasing.

findings.headline: Pay and display parking hosting contracts from 2013 now formalized; Flowbird (£92,910) and International Parking Services (£128,139) arrangements concluded 31 July 2026
findings.detail: Two parking services contracts originated in 2013 without documented procurement. Monthly hosting charges have continued since then, with breaches recorded from 2018 onwards. Competitive procurements were completed and final call-off contracts signed by 31 July 2026, formalizing these arrangements and remediating £221,049 of reported breaches.
findings.matters: Shows control systems identifying and formalizing long-standing loose arrangements; demonstrates proactive management of historic compliance gaps.
findings.figures: £92,910 (Flowbird), £128,139 (International Parking Services); contracts finalized 31 July 2026
findings.quote: A procurement for pay and display machines took place in 2013 although there are no records from the procurement. Since then a monthly hosting charge has been payable but there is no evidence of a compliant procurement to cover this.

findings.headline: Procurement breaches reported for April-July 2026 show considerable reduction in rate and values, with nine breaches totalling £424,468
findings.detail: The council identified nine procurement breaches over four months. The paper reports a considerable reduction in both the rate and values of breaches compared to prior periods. All breaches have been remediated or have remediation underway through compliant procurements, waivers, or contract variations. Controls have been strengthened and staff training implemented to prevent recurrence.
findings.matters: Improving compliance control environment indicates stronger financial governance; peers monitor how other councils manage procurement discipline.
findings.figures: 9 breaches, £424,468 total, April-July 2026
findings.quote: It is apparent that there has been a considerable reduction in the rate of breaches being reported and those reported are generally of a lower value.

findings.headline: Percentage of contract waivers submitted with less than five days' notice fell to 11% from 26%, moving to green and addressing external audit findings on procurement
findings.detail: Waivers submitted less than five days before contract start date fell from 26% in Q4 2025/26 to 11% in Q1 2026/27, meeting the 20% target. The improvement reflects greater emphasis on procurement planning and more time for alternative action should a waiver be denied. This addresses external audit findings that triggered a cross-council drive to promote effective and compliant procurement practice.
findings.matters: Procurement compliance is an audit finding area; improvement shows council is reducing governance risk and responding to external audit concerns, which affects audit opinion and credit assessment.
findings.figures: Late waivers at 11% in Q1 2026/27, down from 26% in Q4 2025/26; target 20%
findings.quote: Performance is now at green, reflecting the greater emphasis on planning for procurement activity and contract management.

findings.headline: Commercial investment portfolio returned 5.26% in Q1 2026/27 against 6% target, with council stating radical review of estate is needed to achieve pathway to target
findings.detail: The council's commercial investment portfolio achieved 5.26% gross return in Q1 2026/27, below the 6% target and rated RED. Commercial properties remain highly occupied, but the council explicitly states that global geopolitical events mean achieving the 6% target is unlikely without major change. A full review of the entire commercial estate is being brought to the October committee. In the interim, officers are considering This Land's future business plan to reduce risk and increase returns, and completing a Kingsbridge rent review.
findings.matters: Commercial investment is material to council finances and forms part of its debt service capacity; acknowledged structural obstacles to meeting return targets and the need for estate review signal potential changes to holdings or strategy that affect the financial position.
findings.figures: 5.26% return against 6% target in Q1 2026/27, up from 4.07% in Q4 2025/26
findings.quote: Global geopolitical events mean it is unlikely the Council will be able to achieve a pathway to achieving 6% going forward without a radical review of the estate.

findings.headline: Multiple public health services under commissioning transition with delivery impact
findings.detail: Behaviour change (smoking cessation) service recommissioning led to recruitment of vacant posts during Q1. Drug and alcohol treatment service recommissioning commenced 1 April 2026. These transitions are affecting near-term performance across multiple public health indicators.
findings.matters: Commissioning disruptions create service continuity risk and workforce recruitment challenges in contracted services; understanding transitions is material to assessing whether performance recovery timelines are realistic.
findings.figures: Drug and alcohol service recommissioning commenced 1 April 2026; vacant posts affecting behaviour change service
findings.quote: activity affected while the provider continues to recruit to vacant posts and establish new clinics

findings.headline: Children in 20% most deprived areas 15 percentage points behind county development average
findings.detail: New indicator shows 72% of 2.5-year-olds in the most deprived areas of Cambridgeshire achieved a good level of development, compared with 87% of all 2.5-year-olds county-wide. Council working with Healthy Child Programme to increase identification and uptake of 2.5-year reviews in deprived families.
findings.matters: Early development gap in deprived areas identifies concentrated service need and predictor of later inequality; targeted early intervention may require additional investment.
findings.figures: 72% (deprived areas) vs 87% (all county); 15 percentage point gap
findings.quote: In the 2025/26 financial year, 72% of 2.5-year-olds from the 20% most deprived areas of the county were assessed as reaching a good level of development, compared with 87% of the whole Cambridgeshire 2.5-year cohort.

findings.headline: Community-based care for older adults improving and outperforming peer councils
findings.detail: The proportion of adults aged 65+ receiving long-term support in their own home or community settings has increased, with fewer requiring residential or nursing care admission. Cambridgeshire compares favourably to statistical neighbours and England overall on this outcome.
findings.matters: Community-based care costs less than residential care, so strong performance signals cost-efficiency and policy effectiveness.
findings.figures: Positive trend vs prior year; favourable comparator position to statistical neighbours and England
findings.quote: A large proportion of adults aged 65+ are having their long-term support needs met in their own home or another community setting with less people needing admission to residential and nursing care homes.

findings.headline: Care home quality increased to 82.4%, exceeding raised target of 81.5%
findings.detail: The proportion of Cambridgeshire care homes rated good or outstanding by CQC has improved to 82.4% at end of Q1, compared to 81.2% in prior quarters and exceeding the increased target of 81.5%. Includes all care homes in the county, not just council-commissioned.
findings.matters: Better care home quality reduces costly investigations, complaints and service failures.
findings.figures: 82.4% vs 81.5% target vs 81.2% previous three quarters
findings.quote: The percentage of Care Homes rated Good or Outstanding by CQC has increased at the end of Q1 to 82.4 which is above the increased target of 81.5% and the prior three quarters of 81.2%.

findings.headline: NHS Health Checks completed at 60% of eligible population against 67.5% target in Q1 2026/27, with recovery actions beginning to show impact
findings.detail: 5,986 health checks completed in Q1 (just over 60% of eligible population) against a 67.5% target. Performance is recovering following introduction of 2026-27 improvement actions, though Healthy You service remains below full capacity. Further improvement expected as service mobilises.
findings.matters: Recovery trajectory suggests improvement actions are taking effect, but underperformance persists and indicates ongoing service capacity constraints.
findings.figures: 5,986 completions; 60% vs 67.5% target; prior quarters showed concerning reduction
findings.quote: A total of 5,986 Health Checks were completed during the quarter, representing uptake of just over 60% of the eligible population. While this remains below the 67.5% target, the increase provides early evidence that the recovery and improvement actions introduced for 2026/27 are beginning to have an impact.

findings.headline: Smoking cessation service at 64% of target, recovering as recommissioning settles
findings.detail: Performance achieved 230 successful quits against a target of 359, improving from 40% of target in Q4 2025-26. Underperformance is attributed to recommissioning disruption with vacant posts and clinic establishment ongoing; improvement expected as provider capacity grows.
findings.matters: Service commissioning risk is constraining public health delivery; workforce recruitment challenges in contracted services delay performance recovery.
findings.figures: 230 quits vs 359 target (64%); up from 40% of target in Q4 2025-26
findings.quote: Performance in Quarter 1 2026/27 achieved 64% of the local target, with 230 people successfully quitting smoking at the four-week stage compared with a target of 359.

findings.headline: Care review backlog continues downward trend despite recent operational improvement
findings.detail: The percentage of people receiving long-term support who had a care review within the last 12 months continues to decline, though February and March showed improvement. The council has conducted demand and capacity reviews and deployed digital tools, but realising performance gains will take time.
findings.matters: Care reviews are a statutory requirement; backlogs create risk of care failures and potential legal non-compliance.
findings.figures: RAG status: Red; trend: downward with recent partial recovery
findings.quote: The number of people who have not received a review of their long-term care and support needs within the last 12 months continues to trend downwards this quarter, although February and March saw an improvement on previous months.

findings.headline: Direct payments to service users remain low against 21% directorate target
findings.detail: The proportion of people receiving direct payments for social care continues to underperform against the directorate target of 21%. The council has recently launched new guidance and initiatives aimed at improving uptake, but the paper does not state the current percentage achieved.
findings.matters: Direct payments increase cost-efficiency and autonomy in social care delivery; underperformance signals implementation barriers or lower-than-expected take-up.
findings.figures: Target: 21%; RAG status: Red
findings.quote: The number of people receiving a Direct Payment continues to remain around low against the directorate target of 21%.

findings.headline: Adult social care locations rated good or outstanding by CQC at 82.4%, above target of 82% and outperforming peer (80.4%) and national (81.2%) averages
findings.detail: Quality of care provision measured through CQC ratings remains above target and above comparator authorities. 82.4% of Cambridgeshire care homes are rated good or outstanding, compared to target of 82.0%, peer mean 80.4%, and national mean 81.2%. Performance has remained steady through 2025-26, indicating quality resilience despite system pressures elsewhere.
findings.matters: Quality assurance remains above average despite demand challenges in other areas; above-target performance signals sustained service quality delivery under pressure
findings.figures: 82.4% rated good or outstanding (Q1 2026-27), target 82.0%, peer mean 80.4%, national mean 81.2%
findings.quote: Performance has remained steady in 2025-26 and overall remains above target and above both peer and national performance.

findings.headline: NHS Health Checks uptake recovered to 60% in Q1 2026-27 from 52% in Q4 2025-26; recovery plan approved with funding for five additional community kiosks from June 2026
findings.detail: Cardiovascular risk checks for ages 40-74 had fallen to 52% in Q4 2025-26, below the 67.5% target. Q1 2026-27 shows recovery to 60%. The council states this provides "early evidence that the recovery and improvement actions introduced for 2026/27 are beginning to have an impact." Recovery plan includes restarted outreach, strengthened GP engagement, targeted training, and approved funding for five self-service kiosks to deploy in supermarkets starting June 2026.
findings.matters: Public health prevention service had declined but is recovering; approved funding for kiosk expansion represents sustained commitment; improvement demonstrates effectiveness of council recovery actions
findings.figures: 60% uptake (Q1 2026-27), target 67.5%, prior quarter 52%, England average 44%, improvement of 8 percentage points quarter-on-quarter
findings.quote: Q1 2026/27 shows a positive improvement in NHS Health Check performance following the concerning reduction seen in the proceeding quarters of 2025/26. While this remains below the 67.5% target, the increase provides early evidence that the recovery and improvement actions introduced for 2026/27 are beginning to have an impact.

findings.headline: Proportion of service users receiving direct payments at 16.5%, below target of 21% and significantly below peer (26.4%) and national (24.5%) averages
findings.detail: Direct payments enable service users to exercise choice and control over how their care needs are met. Q1 2026-27 shows 16.5% of people receiving community long-term support receiving direct payments, against a target of 21%. Performance lags well below both peer neighbours (26.4%) and England (24.5%), suggesting take-up or support barriers. A Task and Finish group has been established to improve practice guidance, website information, and support services, with the directorate aiming to reach target by end of Q4.
findings.matters: Direct payments are a key mechanism for enabling service user choice and cost efficiency; significant underperformance against target and gap with peer authorities indicates implementation challenges; recovery deadline is only three quarters away
findings.figures: 16.5% current (Q1 2026-27), target 21%, peer mean 26.4%, national mean 24.5%, gap to peer average 9.9 percentage points
findings.quote: 16.5% of people receiving community long-term support at the end of the quarter (Q1 2026/27) received direct payments as part of self-directed support. This is compared to a target of 21%.

findings.headline: Emergency hospital admissions due to falls in people aged 65+ increased to 2,148 per 100,000 in 2024-25, continuing upward trend against target of 1,958 per 100,000
findings.detail: Falls are the largest cause of emergency hospital admission for older people and a major precipitant of loss of independence and institutional care placement. The rate has risen from 2,050 per 100,000 in 2023-24 to 2,148 in 2024-25. The council identifies this as sustained system-wide pressure despite strong uptake of existing prevention services. Response includes falls prevention strategy refresh, new Healthy Behaviour Change service from December 2025, and expansion of community provision with funding increased fourfold for universal strength and balance activities starting July 2026.
findings.matters: Rising emergency admissions due to falls represent significant ongoing cost pressure; the council identifies this as sustained system-wide pressure; fourfold funding increase for prevention services indicates the scale of the challenge
findings.figures: 2,148 per 100,000 (2024-25), target 1,958, prior year 2,050, year-on-year increase of 98 per 100,000
findings.quote: The rate has increased from 2050 per 100,000 in 2023/24 to 2148 per 100,000 in 2024/25, indicating a continued upward trend and sustained system pressure.

findings.headline: Statutory annual reviews of long-term care plans completed for only 52% of eligible adults, declining from 58.7% a year earlier, with consistent quarter-on-quarter decline
findings.detail: It is a statutory duty to review long-term care and support plans at least annually. Q1 2026-27 shows 52% reviewed against a target of 60%, having fallen from 58.7% in Q1 2025-26. The council explicitly attributes this to resource constraints. Responses include rollout of Beam Notes system and establishment of a Community Adults Review Team, but improvements are expected to take time while the backlog reduces.
findings.matters: This is a statutory compliance obligation; sustained decline over four consecutive quarters indicates a growing backlog of unreviewed cases; the council explicitly states resource constraints are the cause, indicating cost pressures to resolve the issue
findings.figures: 52% (Q1 2026-27), target 60%, decline from 58.7% one year earlier (Q1 2025-26), continuous decline from 58.7% → 56.3% → 54.6% → 52.0% → 51.5%
findings.quote: Levels of incoming safeguarding and urgent work are impacting on the ability to make improvements.

findings.headline: Forecast underspend of £3,927k (1.5% of budget) at August 2026
findings.detail: The directorate is forecasting an underspend of £3,927k. This reflects what the paper describes as proactive financial management, rigorous oversight of demand-led budgets, successful inflation risk management and delivery of commissioning efficiencies. The current underspend provides financial resilience, though it sits alongside the identified savings delivery challenge.
findings.matters: An underspend demonstrates current financial control and management strength; however, read alongside the £3.1m savings shortfall, it raises the question of whether the strength is structural or dependent on favourable variances that may not recur.
findings.figures: £3,927k underspend; 1.5% of annual budget
findings.quote: The overall position for Adults, Health and Commissioning budgets at the end of August 2026 is a forecast underspend of £3,927k (equivalent to 1.5% of the annual budget).

findings.headline: Adults risk reserves total £4.61m with £2.26m uncommitted at year start
findings.detail: Total risk reserves of £4.61m at the start of 2026-27 comprise £2.18m committed to invest-to-save schemes approved in previous business plans. The section 151 officer has further committed £175k to support transport systems work. This leaves £2.26m uncommitted reserves available to absorb unforeseen pressures.
findings.matters: Uncommitted reserves represent the financial buffer against unexpected demands; at £2.26m, this is less than 1% of the directorate's budget, indicating limited headroom for absorbing additional pressures beyond those already managed.
findings.figures: £4.61m total reserves; £2.18m committed to future schemes; £175k committed to transport systems; £2.26m uncommitted
findings.quote: The balance of Adults risk reserves at the start of 2026-27 totalled £4.61m of which £2.18m is committed to future spend, particularly invest to save schemes approved in recent Business Plans.

findings.headline: Physical Disability services experiencing increasing demand and high-cost placements
findings.detail: Physical Disability is identified as the area facing the most notable financial pressure within Adult Social Care. Increasing demand, greater complexity of need, and a small number of high-cost placements are creating forecast cost pressures. The council is managing these actively through package reviews, strengthened commissioning, and maximising health funding contributions.
findings.matters: Physical disability is typically a high-cost, volatile area of adult social care; the paper identifies it as the point of greatest pressure, which is relevant to understanding sustainability of the current underspend.
findings.figures: Not quantified
findings.quote: The most notable pressure is within Physical Disability services, where increasing demand, greater complexity of need and a small number of high-cost placements are creating forecast cost pressures.

findings.headline: Overdue debt levels remain high in adult social care income collection
findings.detail: Income collection and debt recovery are identified as a key focus area. Despite targeted recovery work being led by Finance and Resources colleagues working with service users, health partners and income collection teams, the paper reports that overdue debt levels remain high.
findings.matters: Persistent high overdue debt in adult social care income directly affects the council's cash flow and revenue position; it indicates either vulnerable service users in arrears or collection system weaknesses, both of which are relevant to a lender assessing the reliability of the revenue base.
findings.figures: Not quantified
findings.quote: Income collection and debt recovery remain a key area of focus. While overdue debt levels remain high, targeted work is underway, led by colleagues in Finance and Resources, with people who draw on care and support, health partners, and income collection teams to improve recovery rates and strengthen the overall income position.

findings.headline: Directorate forecast to deliver £16.2m of a £19.3m savings programme
findings.detail: The directorate is pursuing a savings programme of £19.3m for 2026-27. Current forecasts show delivery of £16.2m, a shortfall of approximately 16%. The paper notes that recovery plans are in place for schemes experiencing delays and that any forecast shortfalls are being mitigated through alternative savings and favourable variances elsewhere.
findings.matters: A 16% shortfall on a major savings programme raises questions about the robustness of the budget plan and the council's capacity to deliver savings; undelivered savings must be offset elsewhere to balance the budget.
findings.figures: £19.3m savings programme; £16.2m forecast delivery
findings.quote: The Directorate is also delivering against a challenging savings programme of £19.3m. Current forecasts indicate delivery of £16.2m, with recovery plans in place for schemes experiencing delays.

findings.paper_title: Item 10 - Appendix 1 - Finance Monitoring Report August 2026
findings.headline: Service Director - Commissioning showing £2m (52%) underspend as provider inflation negotiations conclude and held risk budget releases
findings.detail: Service Director - Commissioning net budget £3.854m forecast to underspend by £2m. Paper commentary states: 'Negotiations with providers over 2026-27 inflationary uplifts are now coming to a conclusion allowing the partial release of the risk budget held back awaiting the outcome of inflation awards.' Position improved month-on-month from -£1.750m previous variance. This release feeds into overall commissioning position.
findings.matters: Provider inflation negotiation completion is material to budget certainty; early resolution signals potential stabilisation of adult social care provider costs.
findings.figures: Service Director - Commissioning: net budget £3.854m, forecast variance -£2.000m (52% underspend), previous month -£1.750m. Improvement of £250k month-on-month.
findings.quote: Negotiations with providers over 2026-27 inflationary uplifts are now coming to a conclusion allowing the partial release of the risk budget held back awaiting the outcome of inflation awards.

findings.paper_title: Item 10 - Appendix 1 - Finance Monitoring Report August 2026
findings.headline: Capital programme: no schemes with forecast variances exceeding £250k threshold
findings.detail: Capital revised budget £7.147m (original £6.690m plus £407k rephasing, minus £81k variations, plus £131k funding adjustments). Actual spend to August £2.294m. Paper states explicitly no significant variances. Schemes include Disabled Facilities Grant (£6.381m), Integrated Community Equipment (£400k), Specialist Accommodation (£407k), IT Systems (£32k).
findings.matters: Capital programme control provides budget stability and demonstrates programme management capability; positive contrast to revenue pressures.
findings.figures: Revised budget £7.147m, actual spend (August) £2.294m, forecast variance £0k.
findings.quote: At the end of August 2026, no capital schemes have significant forecast variances against updated budgets.

findings.paper_title: Item 10 - Appendix 1 - Finance Monitoring Report August 2026
findings.headline: Adults, Health and Commissioning forecasting £3.927m underspend (1.5% of £266.853m net budget)
findings.detail: Despite £1.1m Physical Disabilities overspend, £3.1m savings shortfall, and £602k income under-recovery in Older People's, directorate maintains overall underspend through commissioning efficiencies and underspends in other services. Paper describes position as 'strong' and 'controlled'. Underspend has remained stable month-on-month (was £3.490m in previous month, now £3.927m).
findings.matters: Overall positive position masks underlying pressures that could crystallise if commissioning underspends or mitigation activities prove unsustainable; requires monitoring of what is driving the mitigation.
findings.figures: £3.927m underspend on net budget of £266.853m = 1.5%. Month-on-month movement +£437k from previous £3.490m underspend.
findings.quote: At the end of August 2026, Adults, Health and Commissioning is forecasting an underspend of £3,927k for the 2026-27 financial year equivalent to 1.5% of the annual budget.

findings.paper_title: Item 10 - Appendix 1 - Finance Monitoring Report August 2026
findings.headline: Older People's services showing £602k net pressure from under-recovery of client contribution income; high levels of adult social care debt remain
findings.detail: Despite lower than budgeted activity levels in accommodation-based services (1,448 placements vs 1,406 budgeted), forecast shows £602k under-recovery against budgeted client contributions. Paper flags 'High levels of adult social care debt continue to create uncertainty within the income position and the potential future impact.' Income collection described as 'a key area of focus' with 'targeted work underway'.
findings.matters: Income under-recovery combined with high debt levels indicates either collection difficulties or service user affordability pressures that could deteriorate; material to councils' understanding of income sustainability in adult social care.
findings.figures: Older People's total budget £123.263m gross, £42.452m net after care contributions (budgeted at £44.210m). Variance in care contributions: -£1.758k. £602k net pressure specifically called out in commentary.
findings.quote: While net activity levels for Older People's services remain lower than budgeted, a forecast under-recovery against budgeted income from client contributions is creating a net pressure of £602k. High levels of adult social care debt continue to create uncertainty within the income position and the potential future impact.

findings.paper_title: Item 10 - Appendix 1 - Finance Monitoring Report August 2026
findings.headline: Physical Disabilities services forecast £1.1m overspend: North £833k (11%), South £299k (4%)
findings.detail: Physical Disabilities North shows £833k overspend (11% of net budget £7.256m), South shows £299k overspend (4% of net budget £7.994m), total £1.1m pressure on budget of £17.330m. Paper identifies cause as 'increased demand and complexity of high-cost placements' and notes response includes 'robust package reviews, strengthened commissioning arrangements and maximising health funding contributions where appropriate'. Managing through active interventions but pressure is emerging mid-year.
findings.matters: Unexplained demand pressure is material; indicates potential structural change in service population, costs, or pricing that may persist beyond this year and signal similar pressures in other councils' physical disability services.
findings.figures: Physical Disabilities North: £7.256m net budget, £833k overspend (11% of budget). Physical Disabilities South: £7.994m net budget, £299k overspend (4%). Total Physical Disabilities budget £17.330m.
findings.quote: Within Physical Disabilities, an emerging £1.1m pressure is being driven primarily by increased demand and complexity of high-cost placements.

findings.paper_title: Item 10 - Appendix 1 - Finance Monitoring Report August 2026
findings.headline: Savings programme delivering £16.2m of planned £19.3m target; £3.1m shortfall being mitigated by alternative underspends
findings.detail: Savings tracker shows forecast delivery of £16.2m against planned £19.3m – a 16% shortfall (£3.1m). Multiple schemes are underperforming: Review in-house services (£850k shortfall, 85%), Double Up Care (50% delivery, £350k shortfall), Reablement Physiotherapy (50% delivery, £327k shortfall), Accommodation Supported Living (£204k, 100% undeliverable), Increase Income from Charging multiple schemes (£184k combined undelivered). Paper states shortfalls 'currently being mitigated through alternative savings and favourable variances elsewhere within the budget'.
findings.matters: Savings shortfalls of this magnitude signal delivery risk; a finance director needs to understand whether mitigations are sustainable or whether replacement savings are temporary cash management.
findings.figures: Planned £19.253m, Forecast £16.159m, Variance £3.094m (16%). Amber schemes: £1.067m shortfall. Red schemes: £1.527m shortfall. Black schemes: £500k undeliverable.
findings.quote: Current forecasts indicate delivery of £16.2m, with recovery plans in place for schemes experiencing delays. Any forecast shortfalls are currently being mitigated through alternative savings and favourable variances elsewhere within the budget.

findings.committee: Communities, Social Mobility and Inclusion Committee
findings.headline: Mortuary service demand expected to continue increasing in line with demographic trends
findings.detail: In 2025, 2,765 deaths reported to Coroner with 1,204 requiring post-mortem examination. Demand expected to continue increasing. Contract structured on demand-led, per-case charging basis, meaning actual annual costs will vary with activity. Baseline £1.28m excludes future price uplifts, which will be considered annually at council discretion subject to available funding.
findings.matters: Rising demand creates budget pressure on a non-discretionary statutory service; actual annual costs could exceed baseline if demand continues to increase, requiring council to find additional funding through annual reviews
findings.figures: 2,765 deaths reported to the Coroner, of which 1,204 required a post-mortem examination in 2025; demand expected to continue to increase in line with demographic trends
findings.quote: Demand for the service has remained high and is expected to continue to increase in line with demographic trends and annual case volumes. The actual value of the arrangement will vary depending on activity levels.

findings.committee: Communities, Social Mobility and Inclusion Committee
findings.headline: Three-year mortuary services contract from April 2027 valued at approximately £1.28m over the term
findings.detail: Council proposing three-year contract with North West Anglia NHS Trust commencing April 1, 2027, following expiry of current arrangements on March 31, 2027. Contract includes option to extend for one further year. Estimated value £1.28m over initial three-year term, though actual cost will vary depending on activity levels and demand for the service.
findings.matters: Material multi-year financial commitment for statutory service requiring council budget planning; actual annual costs dependent on activity levels create budget uncertainty
findings.figures: £1.28m over the initial three-year term
findings.quote: The proposed arrangement has an assured value of approximately £1.28m over the initial three-year term. This value does not include any future annual price uplifts.

findings.headline: Planning overspend of £183k forecast linked to enforcement appeal at Goslings Drove and Saxon Pit planning appeal costs
findings.detail: The planning budget is forecasting an overspend of £183k linked to an enforcement appeal at Goslings Drove and anticipated costs arising from the Saxon Pit planning appeal. The position will continue to be monitored throughout the year.
findings.matters: Appeal costs are unpredictable and can escalate; this indicates where planning and enforcement decisions are creating unbudgeted financial obligations.
findings.figures: £183k overspend
findings.quote: Planning: the planning budget is forecasting an overspend of £183k linked to an enforcement appeal at Goslings Drove and anticipated costs arising from the Saxon Pit planning appeal.

findings.headline: Energy Projects overspend of £631k forecast, driven by higher operating costs and lower-than-expected St Ives Park & Ride revenue
findings.detail: Operating costs across all energy schemes are significantly higher than originally forecast, driven mainly by increased operation and maintenance contract costs, higher imported electricity charges and rising insurance premiums. The St Ives Park & Ride scheme is particularly affected, with lower-than-expected revenue generation due to limited EV charging take-up and delays in connecting a direct customer.
findings.matters: Schemes not performing operationally as projected indicate either forecasting weakness or genuine market challenges; the St Ives Park & Ride revenue shortfall is material for debt serviceability and the viability of council capital assumptions.
findings.figures: £631k overspend
findings.quote: Energy Projects: an overspend of £631k is forecast. Operating costs across all energy schemes are significantly higher than originally forecast, driven mainly by increased operation and maintenance contract costs, higher imported electricity charges and rising insurance premiums.

findings.headline: Waste Management underspend of £1.3m has reduced from previous months owing to bulky waste volumes and Energy from Waste contract delays
findings.detail: The waste budget is forecasting an underspend of £1.3m driven by increased diversion of waste from landfill to Energy from Waste treatment and separate food waste collections. However, the underspend has declined from earlier forecasts due to increased volumes of bulky waste received and delays in agreeing an Energy from Waste offtake contract, though higher food waste capture rates may offset some of this impact.
findings.matters: Waste is a major controllable cost for councils; declining underspends indicate emerging pressures that could reverse expected savings and affect financial delivery assumptions.
findings.figures: £1.3m underspend
findings.quote: this has reduced from the underspend forecast in previous months owing to increased volumes of bulky waste received and delays in agreeing an Energy from Waste offtake contract.

findings.committee: Communities, Social Mobility and Inclusion Committee
findings.headline: Cambridgeshire Local Assistance Scheme core budget substituted with Crisis and Resilience Fund, releasing £311k
findings.detail: The Anti-Poverty service has replaced its core revenue budget for the Local Assistance Scheme with funding from the Crisis and Resilience Fund. This substitution releases £311k which contributes towards the council's overall financial position and is the key issue reported for this committee's 2026-27 financial performance.
findings.matters: A significant change in how a core service is funded suggests the council is using non-core funding sources to meet spending commitments, which raises questions about sustainability if the Crisis and Resilience Fund is temporary.
findings.figures: £311k saving
findings.quote: Core revenue budget that funds the Cambridgeshire Local Assistance Scheme has been substituted by funding from the Crisis and Resilience Fund, releasing a saving of £311k which contributes towards the Council's overall financial position.

findings.headline: County Matters planning applications determined on time at 100% in Q1 2026-27
findings.detail: All county matters planning applications were determined within required timeframes in Q1, maintaining 100% performance through strong procedural controls and electronic tracking systems.
findings.matters: Consistent on-time determination of planning applications avoids reputational damage and potential penalties, and demonstrates reliable service delivery
findings.figures: 100% of applications determined within required timeframes
findings.quote: As of June 2026, performance remains at 100%, demonstrating strong operational control and risk mitigation.

findings.headline: All major planning project deadlines met in Q1 2026-27
findings.detail: The council achieved 100% performance in meeting Planning Inspectorate and developer deadlines for major infrastructure projects. These included East Park Energy Examination, East West Rail consultation response, Kingsway Solar Farm, and Medworth Energy from Waste Combined Heat and Power Facility.
findings.matters: Meeting statutory deadlines in major infrastructure projects avoids penalties from the Secretary of State and maintains the council's credibility and influence in national infrastructure decisions
findings.figures: 100% of deadlines met
findings.quote: As of June 2026, performance shows all deadlines met, including East Park Energy Examination, responding to the East West Rail consultation, Kingsway Solar Farm, and Medworth Energy from Waste Combined Heat and Power Facility.

findings.headline: Municipal waste landfilled decreased to 34.8% and recycling rate improved to 58.6% in 12 months to March 2026
findings.detail: The proportion of waste sent to landfill fell to 34.8% from previous levels as waste was diverted to energy recovery. The combined recycling, reuse, composting and recovery rate improved to 58.6%, an increase on earlier periods, reflecting operational improvements in waste diversion since summer 2025.
findings.matters: Waste management and disposal costs are material council expenses; reducing landfill use and improving recovery rates both reduce operational costs and support the council's environmental objectives
findings.figures: 34.8% waste landfilled (decrease from previous quarter); 58.6% recycled, reused, composted or recovered (improvement on previous periods)
findings.quote: During the latest 12-month period ending March 2026, 34.8% of waste was landfilled, a decrease since the previous quarter, reflecting increased levels of waste diverted from landfill to energy recovery from summer 2025 onwards.

findings.headline: North Angle Solar Farm subject to grid curtailment reducing output at peak demand periods
findings.detail: North Angle operates under a flexible grid connection allowing UK Power Networks to reduce or switch off the farm's output when excessive power is being generated on the network. The council notes that output continues to be closely monitored and officers are liaising with UK Power Networks and O&M contractors to optimise performance.
findings.matters: Curtailment directly reduces electricity generation and therefore revenue from the £34.058m capital investment, contributing to the identified £344k budget pressure and creating forecasting uncertainty
findings.figures: 29.4MW installed capacity; 22.6GWh generated in first year (subsequently affected by curtailment events)
findings.quote: This can result in the solar farm experiencing curtailment, being turned down or switched off, for a period of time.

findings.headline: Operations and maintenance contracts for both solar farms valued at £4.4m over four years; procurement scheduled for completion in September 2027
findings.detail: Cambridgeshire will conduct a competitive procurement for new O&M contracts for North Angle and Triangle Solar Farms with a total expected value of approximately £4.4m (including VAT) over a 4-year initial term with two optional 1-year extensions. Current contracts expire February 2028 (North Angle) and March 2028 (Triangle). Market testing and procurement documentation preparation is scheduled for February-July 2027, with contract award anticipated in September 2027.
findings.matters: O&M costs at this scale directly impact the financial viability and net returns of the council's renewable energy portfolio
findings.figures: £4.4m over 4-year term including VAT; current contracts expire February-March 2028; procurement timeline February-September 2027
findings.quote: The total value of the contracts is expected to be around £4.4m (inc. VAT) over the proposed 4-year term with 2 one-year extension options.

findings.headline: North Angle Solar Farm has £344k identified revenue budget pressure due to O&M contract costs and curtailment-related income reduction
findings.detail: North Angle Solar Farm, which began operating in November 2024 with a capital investment of £34.058m, generated £1.96m income in its first full year (2025/26). The council has identified a revenue budget pressure of £344k, attributed to current O&M contract costs combined with reduced income from curtailment experienced in the previous year.
findings.matters: A £344k pressure on a major council capital asset indicates the financial model requires active management and forecasting income from assets subject to grid curtailment is more complex than anticipated
findings.figures: £344k identified pressure; £1.96m income 2025/26; £34.058m capital investment; 22.6GWh first year generation
findings.quote: the Council currently has an identified pressure within the revenue budget of £344k due to the current O&M contract costs set against a reduced income due to curtailment experienced in the previous year

findings.headline: Place and Sustainability overall underspend of £3,223k narrowing: decreased by £540k from July as pressures emerge
findings.detail: Directorate forecasting £3,223k underspend (3.7% of £86.814m net budget) at end of August, down from £3,763k in July. Tightening position month-on-month suggests emerging pressures offsetting earlier underspends.
findings.matters: Overall position positive but trajectory is deteriorating; month-on-month reduction of £540k indicates pressures accelerating; would alert finance director to need for tighter monitoring.
findings.figures: £3,223k underspend (3.7%); decrease of £540k on July position
findings.quote: At the end of August 2026, Place and Sustainability is forecasting an underspend of -£3,223k, a decrease of £540k on the underspend reported in July.

findings.headline: Savings delivery: Street lighting energy savings over-performing (£1.785m vs £301k plan) but Highways Development Management income £154k unmet
findings.detail: Q1 savings tracker shows street lighting delivering £1.485m more than plan (blue rating), but Highways Development Management income saving only delivering £398k of £552k target (red rating) with £154k shortfall despite ongoing review.
findings.matters: Mixed delivery on savings: operational savings over-delivering but income-dependent savings at risk; Highways income pressure suggests market or licensing assumptions not holding; typical tracker trend for councils with income-dependent savings targets.
findings.figures: Street lighting: £1,785k actual vs £301k plan; Highways Development Management: £398k actual vs £552k plan (£154k shortfall, 28% variance)
findings.quote: Street lighting energy savings -301 -1,785 -1,484 -493% Blue Saving over-delivered

findings.headline: Anti-Poverty service funding model changed: Cambridgeshire Local Assistance Scheme switched from core budget to Household Support Fund, releasing £311k saving
findings.detail: Core revenue budget funding the Cambridgeshire Local Assistance Scheme has been substituted with Household Support Fund, releasing £311k saving to support council's financial position. Service continues but on grant funding rather than core budget.
findings.matters: Service continues but funding moved from permanent core budget to time-limited grant (Household Support Fund); creates future year funding risk if grant ends; lender would want clarity on contingency if grant ceases.
findings.figures: £311k saving (23% of Anti-Poverty budget)
findings.quote: Core revenue budget that funds the Cambridgeshire Local Assistance Scheme has been substituted by funding from the Household Support Fund, releasing a saving of £311k to support the council's overall financial position.

findings.headline: Capital scheme 'Safer Routes to Schools' paused following local member objection, creating £580k capital underspend
findings.detail: Highways and Transport capital forecasting £580k underspend from halting one of the larger 'safer routes to schools' projects after objection from local members. Other schemes will progress but unlikely to be delivered before 2027-28. Underspend is within capital variations budget, keeping overall capital programme at breakeven.
findings.matters: Stakeholder objection causing capital scheme delay and rephasing; cash flow impact pushed into next year; indicates governance/member engagement issues on delivery.
findings.figures: £580k underspend on Safety Schemes capital project
findings.quote: This underspend is on the Safety schemes project and is due to halting one of the larger 'safer routes to schools' projects following objection from local members.

findings.headline: Planning budget forecasting £183k overspend due to costs of enforcement and planning appeals at Goslings Drove and Saxon Pit
findings.detail: Planning budget (17% overspend) facing cost pressures from enforcement appeal at Goslings Drove and anticipated further pressure from Saxon Pit planning appeal. Being reviewed regularly to assess likelihood of further cost escalation during financial year.
findings.matters: Appeal costs are not fully predictable and may worsen; appeals are legal obligations creating contingent costs; councils with similar enforcement caseloads would recognise this pressure.
findings.figures: £183k overspend (17% of £1,095k net budget)
findings.quote: The current forecast is based on anticipated costs linked to an enforcement appeal at Goslings Drove and a further pressure anticipated for the Saxon Pit planning appeal.

findings.headline: Waste Management underspend of £1.3m revised down from previous forecast due to increased bulky waste volumes and Energy from Waste contract delays
findings.detail: Waste budget forecasting £1.3m underspend from diversion to Energy from Waste treatment and separate food waste collections, but this has reduced from earlier forecasts. Increased bulky waste volumes and delays in agreeing EfW offtake contract are pressures, partially offset by higher-than-predicted food waste capture rates.
findings.matters: Strategic waste diversion programme delivering savings but savings trajectory is declining month-on-month; contract negotiation delays indicate commercial risk; waste composition changes (higher bulky volumes) affecting returns.
findings.figures: £1.3m underspend (revised down from earlier forecast)
findings.quote: The waste budget is forecasting a revised underspend of £1.3m. The underspend is linked to expected savings from increased diversion of waste from landfill to Energy from Waste treatment and the introduction of separate food waste collections. However, this has reduced from the underspend forecast in previous months owing to increased volumes of bulky waste received and delays in agreeing an Energy from Waste offtake contract.

findings.headline: Street Lighting energy savings delivering £1,785k underspend against £301k planned as LED rollout reduces consumption to half prior year levels
findings.detail: LED lantern replacement project driving significant underspend of £1,972k (21% of budget) with year-to-date electricity usage approximately half that of prior year. Additional savings from annual electricity charge adjustment (May 2026), PFI contract pension reconciliation (July 2026), and LED-related maintenance savings. Street lighting energy savings line is delivering £1,785k forecast against £301k plan.
findings.matters: Operational improvement from capital investment (LED rollout) delivering savings greater than plan; demonstrates council's ability to convert infrastructure investment into revenue savings; ongoing benefit expected as rollout continues.
findings.figures: £1,972k underspend; year-to-date usage approximately half prior year; street lighting energy savings delivering £1,785k against £301k plan (493% over-delivery)
findings.quote: Savings reflect reduced energy consumption from the ongoing LED lantern replacement project. Year to date usage is approximately half that of the same period in the prior year.

findings.headline: Energy Projects forecasting £631k overspend driven by higher operational costs and lower revenue from St Ives Park & Ride
findings.detail: Energy schemes facing cost pressures from increased operation & maintenance contract costs, higher imported electricity charges, and rising insurance premiums. St Ives Park & Ride scheme particularly affected by lower-than-expected revenue due to limited EV charging take-up and delays in customer connection. This represents 42% of the net budget.
findings.matters: Revenue-earning council asset not generating expected income; operational cost inflation suggests ongoing pressure; lender would want to know energy investment returns are below plan.
findings.figures: £631k overspend (42% of £1,513k net budget)
findings.quote: Operating costs across all energy schemes are significantly higher than originally forecast, driven mainly by increased operation & maintenance contract costs, higher imported electricity charges and rising insurance premiums. For the St Ives Park & Ride scheme, the impact is exacerbated by lower-than-expected revenue generation, as a result of limited EV charging take up and delays associated with the connection of a direct customer.

findings.headline: Council has identified further Scope 3 emissions reduction actions but notes an emissions gap where additional actions remain unidentified to reach its 2030 target
findings.detail: The council reports Scope 3 emissions of 123,647 tonnes CO2e (down 32% from 2018 baseline) and has identified specific actions including schools decarbonisation and highways decarbonisation. However, commentary states that an emissions gap exists despite these identified actions, requiring further reduction actions that remain unidentified to reach the 2030 target. The report also notes uncertainty around future construction levels which could widen the gap.
findings.matters: An identified strategic commitment (37.8% emissions reduction by 2030) without yet-identified delivery actions or funding signals a future spending requirement that finance directors need to track as an unfunded liability.
findings.figures: 123,647 tonnes Scope 3 emissions (current); 37.8% reduction target by 2030; 32% reduction achieved to date from 2018 baseline
findings.quote: An emissions gap exists however, where further reduction actions as yet unidentified are required to reach the Scope 3 target by 2030.

findings.headline: New waste offtake contract has diverted up to 32% of waste to Energy from Waste facilities, reducing landfill disposal from 35.9% to 34.8%
findings.detail: The council implemented a new offtake contract in 2025-26 that routes waste to Energy from Waste (EfW) rather than landfill. The report notes this has caused a significant fall in waste sent to landfill throughout 2025-26. Waste management is explicitly identified as having significant financial impact on the council, and this material change in disposal routing directly affects the council's waste management cost base.
findings.matters: Waste is a major council expenditure. A change in the proportion of waste sent to landfill versus energy recovery changes the disposal cost structure and affects the waste budget.
findings.figures: 34.8% (current landfill proportion) vs 35.9% (previous); up to 32% of waste diverted to Energy from Waste
findings.quote: Significant fall throughout 25/26, due to new offtake contract diverting up to 32% of waste from landfill to Energy from Waste (EfW)
